 More than 720K BMW vehicles recalled over fire threat, regulators say
 Owners are instructed to park vehicles outside and away from structures until a remedy is completed
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 Threads 
 Print 
 Email 
 Add Fox Business on Google 
 By Landon Mion FOXBusiness close video BMW recalls 720,000 cars as water-pump defect creates fire risk 
 BMW is recalling 720,796 vehicles over a faulty water-pump electrical connector that can short-circuit and cause a fire, even while the cars are parked and turned off.
 More than 720,000 BMW vehicles are facing a recall over a defect that could cause a fire "while parked and turned off," according to federal regulators.
 BMW is recalling 720,796 vehicles due to faulty water pumps that could short-circuit, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) said in its notice.
 The recall affects certain 2012–2016 BMW 3 Series, 5 Series and Z4 vehicles; 2012–2015 X1 models; 2013–2017 X3 models; 2015–2016 4 Series Gran Coupe and 2 Series Convertible models; 2014–2016 328xi Gran Turismo, 2 Series Coupe, 4 Series Convertible, 3 Series Coupe and 3 Series Sportswagon models; 2015–2018 X4 models; and 2016–2018 X5 xDrive40e vehicles.
 HONDA RECALLS MORE THAN 635,000 VEHICLES OVER STEERING DEFECT THAT INCREASES CRASH RISK 
 More than 720,000 BMW vehicles are facing a recall over a defect that could cause a fire, according to federal regulators. (Getty Images / Getty Images) 
 "An improperly sealed electrical connector on the water pump may be exposed to water and short circuit," the NHTSA notice reads.
 The NHTSA notice warns that a short circuit could increase the risk of a fire.
 "Over time, due to material degradation at the connector, this could allow moisture to enter the pump and lead to the possibility of a short circuit," the agency wrote.
 BMW is recalling 720,796 vehicles due to faulty water pumps that could short-circuit. (Raymond Boyd/Michael Ochs Archives/Getty Images / Getty Images) 
 "This could increase the risk of a thermal event and, in rare cases, a fire," it added.
 BMW is aware of about 10 potentially related incidents in the U.S., involving vehicles previously repaired under the 2024 recall, the NHTSA said. The automaker has not received reports of any accidents or injuries related to the issue.
 The recall replaces a 2024 recall involving previously recalled vehicles. Vehicles repaired under the earlier recall will require an additional repair, according to NHTSA.
 TOYOTA RECALLS 31,000 RAV4 PLUG-IN HYBRIDS THAT MAY SHUT DOWN AT HIGH SPEEDS 
 BMW is aware of about 10 field instances in the U.S. market linked to the defect. (Matthias Balk/picture alliance via Getty Images / Getty Images) 
 GET FOX BUSINESS ON THE GO BY CLICKING HERE 
 Vehicle owners are instructed to park their vehicles outside and away from structures until the recall remedy is completed. The remedy remains under development.
 Owner notification letters are expected to be mailed out beginning Dec. 25, 2026.
 Owners can contact BMW at 800-525-7417 for additional information. Repairs will be provided free of charge once a remedy becomes available.
